chunks: Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “Is the believer afflicted with leprosy, vitiligo, and the like of this?” He said: “And has affliction been written for any except the believer?”

key_terms.الْبَرَصِ: vitiligo or leukoderma, a visible skin affliction
key_terms.الْبَلَاءُ: affliction, trial, or hardship decreed for testing
key_terms.الْجُذَامِ: leprosy, mentioned as a severe bodily affliction
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer, the person characterized by iman
key_terms.كُتِبَ: has been prescribed or written, indicating divine decree

ai.seo_question: Can a believer be afflicted with severe illnesses like leprosy or vitiligo?
ai.summary: This hadith states that severe afflictions can befall the believer and presents such trial as especially associated with the muʾmin. Its significance is that worldly suffering does not negate faith; rather, affliction is portrayed as part of the believer’s divinely written test.
